name: Autoplay
description: Autoplay for level showcases: plans a route while it plays, plays GDR / xdBot macros and runs shared on the global brain. Test mode: nothing is saved as progress. github.com/ilovechubbyorangecat/-predictive-input-buffer

autoplay-label.name: Autoplay Label
autoplay-label.description: The AUTOPLAY label is always on screen while autoplay plays, so a recording can't pass as a real run. Big: at the top. Small: a small see-through label in the bottom corner, for showcases.

autoplay-trail.name: Show Autoplay Trail
autoplay-trail.description: Draws the path autoplay plans (and its inputs) on the level. Off for clean showcase recordings; autoplay plays the same either way.

global-brain.name: Global Brain
global-brain.description: When autoplay finishes a level from its start, the run is shared with the Click Before Frames server (the level, its exact version, your TPS and the button presses; nothing about you), and autoplay plays runs other games finished before looking on Hyperbolus. Off: nothing is sent or used.

online-macros.name: Online Macros (Hyperbolus)
online-macros.description: When autoplay has no macro of yours for a level, it downloads one from Hyperbolus (hyperbolus.net, used with its owner's permission; macros by their uploaders, credited in the log and the autoplay panel). It's saved in the mod's macros folder and replayed from the next attempt. Off: nothing is downloaded.

macro-fixes.name: Macro Position Fixes
macro-fixes.description: When a macro has the bot's position records (xdBot macros do), autoplay keeps you on the macro's path: a small difference in height or angle is set back to the recorded one each step, as xdBot does when it plays its macros. Off: the macro's inputs only.

macro-auto-tps.name: Macro Plays At Its TPS
macro-auto-tps.description: A macro made at another TPS (like 360) is played at that TPS while autoplay plays it, exactly like on the bot that made it. Off: it's played by position at your TPS instead (less exact).

macro-xdbot-mode.name: Play xdBot Macros Like xdBot
macro-xdbot-mode.description: An xdBot macro is played exactly the way xdBot plays it: by its own frame count (level time), its inputs and position records applied after the game's step, with nothing else mixed in. Off: autoplay's own way (shift trials, the macro guard, planning around deaths).

macro-offset.name: Macro Timing Offset (steps)
macro-offset.description: Moves every macro input this many physics steps earlier (+) or later (-). Leave at 0 unless a macro that should work dies early on: try 1 or -1.

tps.name: Physics TPS
tps.description: Physics steps per second in levels. 240 is the normal game. Higher values change the physics, so runs at anything but 240 aren't legit completions. Autoplay's planning scales with it automatically, and a macro made at another TPS can be played at its own (Macro Plays At Its TPS).

sim-budget-ms.name: Planning time budget (ms)
sim-budget-ms.description: The most time per frame autoplay spends planning its route (it uses less while frames are slow). Higher = it plans further and finds ways through hard parts sooner, but may drop frames on dense levels.

predict-move-triggers.name: Predict move triggers
predict-move-triggers.description: Spikes, blocks and orbs that a trigger ahead will move are predicted the way the game will move them: move triggers (offset, duration, easing), rotate triggers (spinning around their center group or in place), toggle triggers that switch a group off or on, and spawn triggers, followed through their delays to the move / rotate / toggle triggers they set off (also spawns the game already started with a delay). Moves / rotations already in progress follow their real path. Plain triggers only: target / follow / aim modes and lock to player / camera aren't predicted, touch triggers only once they've fired, and spawn triggers with random delays, remaps or ordered spawning aren't followed. The mod also checks itself: when a real trigger moves something, it compares the result with what it would have predicted, and turns this off for the level if it keeps being wrong.

predict-moving-objects.name: Predict moving objects (experimental)
predict-moving-objects.description: Spikes, saws and blocks near the path that are moving right now (move / rotate triggers) are moved along their current motion while autoplay plans: straight lines, curved / circular paths and spinning. Easing (speeding up / slowing down) isn't predicted.

predict-through-portals.name: Predict through portals
predict-through-portals.description: Autoplay's hidden player keeps going through mode portals (cube, ship, ball, UFO, wave, robot, spider, swing) and switches mode there, instead of its look-ahead stopping at the portal. Teleport portals move it to the orange end, after a solo portal only P1 goes on, and after a dual portal P2 appears with P1, upside down, and both go on. Teleports with forces / redirects / gravity changes still stop it. Turn off if routes around portals look wrong.

online-players.name: Count Me As Online
online-players.description: Counts you in the number of Autoplay players online. Every 90 seconds the game sends the Click Before Frames server an anonymous random id, your device type and the mod's version. No name, account, level or gameplay. Turn it off and nothing is sent.

check-updates.name: Check for updates
check-updates.description: On game start, check GitHub for a newer version and show a popup on the main menu if there is one. 'Update now' downloads it from the latest GitHub release and installs it; restart the game to use it.

bind-menu.name: Key: open menu
bind-menu.description: Opens the Autoplay window, in a level or in the menus. It is the only way to open it. Change it here or in Geode's keybinds popup.

bind-export.name: Key: copy console log
bind-export.description: Works inside a level. Change it here or in Geode's keybinds popup.

bind-console.name: Key: show / hide console
bind-console.description: Works inside a level. Change it here or in Geode's keybinds popup.

drift-check.name: Route step check (debug)
drift-check.description: Every 8th physics step, autoplay's hidden player plays your last step again and the log says where its result differs from yours. Use it (with the copy-log key) to see how precise the predictions are on a level.

explain-inputs.name: Log trigger checks (debug)
explain-inputs.description: Log every self-check of the trigger prediction: whether a real trigger moved its objects the way the mod would have predicted, and by how much it was off. Busy log.

debug-console.name: Debug console window
debug-console.description: Also open a separate Windows console with the same log as the in-game console. Needs a restart.
